newsitem.title: HONG KONG: SEA says Conrad Hotel deal terminated.
newsitem.headline: SEA says Conrad Hotel deal terminated.

text.p: SEA Holdings Ltd said on Monday an agreement reached in December on buying an 80 percent stake of the Conrad Hotel on Hong Kong island for HK$1.85 million from Conrad International Investment Corp (CIIC) had been terminated.

CIIC sent a notice to Gradplus International Ltd (GIL), a 60 percent indirectly-owned subsidiary of SEA Holdings, on January 8 terminating the agreement. All payments were returned with interest, SEA said in a statement.
SEA Holdings did not disclose reasons for the termination but it said a further announcement would be made if necessary to keep shareholders appraised of future developments.
The 531 room hotel with a gross floor area of 552,750 sq ft is owned by Greenroll Ltd..
CIIC has a 30 percent interest in Greenroll while Taiwan-based Pacific Electric Wire and Cable Co and Swire Pacific Ltd unit Swire Properties Ltd, hold 50 and 30 percent stakes, respectively.
CIIC earlier said it would exercise its right of pre-emption to buy 50 percent Greenroll from Pacific Electric Wire bringing its stake in Conrad to 80 percent.
However the SEA agreement came after Sino Hotels (Holdings) Ltd reached a conditional agreement in November to buy 50 percent of Greenroll Ltd for about HK$1.1 billion from Pacific Electric.
Sino Hotels (Holdings) had said it was seeking legal advice concerning the proposed acquisition following the new offer.
